code:
CNOT|00> = |00>    (control 0, target untouched)
CNOT|01> = |01>    (control 0, target untouched)
CNOT|10> = |11>    (control 1, target flips)
CNOT|11> = |10>    (control 1, target flips)
caption: Only the target's bit ever changes, and only where the control bit is 1.

steps.label: CNOT² = I
steps.sub: Apply it twice under the same condition and you undo the first flip exactly

steps.label: CNOT is not "X on both qubits"
steps.sub: X⊗X flips both qubits unconditionally, on every input

steps.label: CNOT can't be factored into two single-qubit gates
steps.sub: That non-factorizability is exactly what lets it entangle

steps.label: CNOT on any of the 4 basis states outputs a basis state
steps.sub: Never a superposition — just a relabeling

steps.label: A basis state is already separable
steps.sub: No uncertainty exists yet to be correlated

steps.label: CNOT alone, fed a basis state, creates no entanglement
steps.sub: CNOT|10⟩ = |11⟩ is still just as separable as the input

steps.label: Entanglement needs a superposition on the control
steps.sub: That's exactly the setup Lesson 13 builds toward

subtitle: CNOT is one instance of a recipe that builds a controlled version of any gate.
